subject: Critical-account availability variance: Aperture Analytics - ops & approval thread
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Team —

Aperture (Elena copied) is asking for a short-term availability variance for a strategic pilot. Key points:
- Ask: 99.99% availability commitment during US business hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT) for 6 months, starting Nov 15.
- Traffic: heavy short bursts (spikes to ~3x baseline) for 2–3 hours/day during client batch windows.
- Impact: they want the commitment to be SLA-backed (credits if not met) and operational runbook.

Attachments: aperture-sla-ask-v1.pdf (customer ask).

Can you two help estimate operational impact (capacity, monitoring, fallback) and list must-have conditions for approvals? I want to pull together an internal approval packet for finance/legal/ops by Friday.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Vivek —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick clarifying Qs before we quantify:
1) Is Aperture on Hosted or Dedicated today? (billing/overprovisioning differs)
2) Are the peak windows predictable by clock time or event-driven?
3) Do they require synchronous tail-latency guarantees (e.g., 95th/99th) or only uptime/availability with credits?

Operational asks we will need from them:
- Expected qps distribution over 24h (CSV or link to heatmap)
- P95/P99 per-endpoint latency targets during the committed window
- Whitelist IPs / network constraints for private callbacks if any

If they're hosted, we can often meet the ask with autoscale + caching + a reserved burst pool; if dedicated, we need to validate capacity headroom. I can draft the conditional pricing uplift after we get the traffic artifacts.

Marissa
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts

(On a separate note: looping Stephanie / David for finance/legal and infra engineering checks.)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Marissa / Vivek —

I pulled their telemetry for the last 90 days (Elena shared read-only links). Summary:
- Baseline qps: 120 req/s across their main model. Peak windows spike to 360 req/s for 1–3 hours, typically 11:30–13:00 PT and 15:00–16:00 PT. See attached: traffic-heatmap-q3.png.
- Current latency p95: ~140ms, p99: ~420ms. Under spikes p99 breaches 800–1,200ms.
- We estimate to hold sub300ms p99 at spike levels we'd need ~25–30% more GPU headroom plus KV cache priming.

Operational caveats:
- If this remains hosted, KV cache warmup during sudden bursts causes temporary p99 regressions. We can mitigate with pre-warming heuristics in the runbook.
- If they want hard latency SLA, recommend dedicated capacity or an explicit pre-warm schedule.

I've uploaded an ops-runbook draft (ops-runbook-aperture.xlsx) with pre-warm steps and alert thresholds.

Grace
Senior SRE, Redwood Console
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aperture.ai>, contracts@aperture.ai
Date: 2027-10-30T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Vivek / team —

From a commercial and legal perspective: we can consider a bounded availability variance with credits, but with the following constraints:
- Term limited to 6 months with a 30-day formal review clause.
- Uptime credit formula must cap total exposure (we will propose cap not to exceed 10% of monthly invoice unless escalated).
- Price uplift: preliminary estimate is +22–30% on token/throughput fees depending on whether they choose hosted (with pre-warm) vs reserved Dedicated. Final numbers subject to Finance sign-off.
- Legal needs the SLA language redline before we send to Aperture. Please push the ops-runbook and final traffic CSV.

Elena — can Aperture confirm willingness to accept a cap on credits and a runbook with pre-warm windows? Also confirm billing account (hosted vs dedicated).

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Commercial Operations
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Team —

Engineering check: we can support a 99.99% availability commitment during the business-hours window with these operational controls in place:
- Reserved burst pool: provision 20% reserved capacity scoped to Aperture (isolated pool on hosted infra) during committed hours.
- Pre-warm API: Aperture must hit a pre-warm endpoint 15–30 minutes before expected spike windows (we include fallback heuristics if they miss pre-warm).
- Fallback policy: if capacity pressured, route to quantized model variant for degraded latency but maintain availability (customer must accept output-quality variance during fallback).
- Monitoring: synthetic p95/p99 checks and automated paging to oncall with a 5-minute escalator.

I'll add a short-runbook section for automated scaling knobs. Also note: the reserved pool increases our operational cost; link to Stephanie for pricing uplift.

-David
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aperture.ai>, contracts@aperture.ai
Date: 2027-11-01T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability variance for Aperture Analytics (high-frequency inference window)

Thanks everyone — alignment summary and next steps: 

1) We will provision a 20% reserved burst pool during Aperture's committed windows and require Aperture to call the pre-warm API 15–30m before spikes.
2) SLA will be limited to business hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT), term = 6 months, 30-day review. Credits capped per month; Stephanie to finalize formula.
3) Fallback to a quantized model variant will be used under pressure; customer accepts potential quality variance.

Action items:
- Grace: finalize ops-runbook (ops-runbook-aperture.xlsx) and link the synthetic checks (due 2027-11-05).
- David: add scaling automation knobs and confirm rollout steps for reserved pool (due 2027-11-04).
- Marissa / Stephanie: finalize pricing uplift and legal redlines; prepare DocuSign for signature (Stephanie to own).
- Marissa: confirm customer acceptance of credit cap and fallback behavior.

Attachments: aperture-sla-draft-v3.docx (internal SLA draft), ops-runbook-aperture.xlsx, traffic-heatmap-q3.png. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/AP-4529.

If there are no objections by EOW I will mark this as approved to move to legal for final redline.

-Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
